stories.title: EU will mandate labels on authentic-looking AI content starting August 2
stories.paragraph: The European Union will require labels on AI-generated content that appears authentic starting August 2, under rules stemming from the EU AI Act. The mandate targets synthetic media that could mislead viewers — such as deepfakes and AI-generated images — by requiring clear disclosure at the point of presentation. This marks one of the first concrete enforcement-level requirements from the EU's broad AI regulatory framework to take effect with a specific compliance date.

stories.title: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
stories.paragraph: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, the latest model in its V4 family, with 304 billion parameters and a file size of 167 GB on Hugging Face. The model is described as having substantially enhanced agentic capabilities and is priced at $0.14 per million input tokens and $0.27 per million output tokens. Artificial Analysis ranks it ahead of MiniMax M3, a 428-billion-parameter model, suggesting strong performance relative to its size and cost.

stories.title: Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science
stories.paragraph: OpenAI published results on ten long-standing open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, covering areas including geometry, cryptography, and complexity theory. The release highlights specific instances where AI-assisted reasoning produced new results rather than reproductions of known solutions. This follows a broader trend of AI systems being applied to formal mathematical research, with OpenAI positioning these findings as contributions to open scientific problems rather than benchmark demonstrations.

stories.title: Stateless MCP has recaptured my interest (and inspired mcp-explorer and datasette-mcp)
stories.paragraph: The Model Context Protocol specification was updated to version 2026-07-28, colloquially called MCP 2.0 or Stateless MCP, representing the most significant revision since the protocol launched. The stateless design eliminates the need for persistent server connections, which Simon Willison describes as reigniting his interest in the protocol and prompting him to build two new tools: mcp-explorer and datasette-mcp. MCP defines a standard interface for exposing data and tools to AI models, and the stateless approach is expected to simplify deployment and integration.

stories.title: llm-mcp-client 0.1a0
stories.paragraph: Simon Willison released llm-mcp-client 0.1a0, an alpha-stage plugin that adds Model Context Protocol client support to his LLM command-line tool. The release coincides with the rollout of the updated stateless MCP specification and is intended to allow LLM users to connect to MCP servers directly from the tool. As an alpha release, the package is available for early testing but is not considered production-ready.

stories.title: Flint: A Visualization Language for the AI Era
stories.paragraph: Microsoft released Flint, a declarative visualization language designed to make chart creation more accessible to AI code-generation systems. Unlike existing charting libraries that rely on imperative JavaScript APIs, Flint uses a structured specification format intended to be easier for language models to produce correctly. The project is hosted on Microsoft's GitHub and positions itself as an alternative to tools like Vega-Lite, tailored for workflows where AI generates the visualization code.

stories.title: Oxide and Friends: The Open Weight Revolution with Simon Willison
stories.paragraph: Simon Willison appeared on the Oxide and Friends podcast hosted by Bryan Cantrill and Adam Leventhal to discuss recent developments in open-weight AI models, including Kimi K3, which he described as demonstrating that open-weight models can compete with proprietary frontier systems. The conversation also covered an accidental cybersecurity incident related to model releases and a public letter on open weights and American AI leadership that gathered signatures from figures across the political spectrum. The episode reflects a week of unusually dense activity in the open-weight model ecosystem.

stories.title: Zitron: "Everyone Has Been Sold a Lie" on AI [video]
stories.paragraph: Tech critic Ed Zitron published a video arguing that the mainstream narrative around AI's economic and productivity benefits is fundamentally misleading. Zitron, who has written extensively about what he calls hype cycles in the tech industry, contends that concrete evidence of large-scale productivity gains remains thin despite significant enterprise investment. The video surfaced on Hacker News and generated discussion about the gap between AI's marketed capabilities and documented real-world outcomes.

stories.title: Google Just Ruined One of Its Most Important Tools
stories.paragraph: The Atlantic reports that Google has introduced AI-generated imagery into Google Earth, replacing or supplementing some satellite photographs with synthetic images. Critics argue this undermines Google Earth's core value as a factual, observable record of the planet's surface, making it harder to distinguish real geographic data from generated content. The change is notable because Google Earth has historically been used by journalists, researchers, and governments as an evidentiary tool for verifying real-world locations and events.

stories.title: AI doesn't generate working products, that's still your job
stories.paragraph: A blog post by Manura Weeraman argues that AI coding tools can produce functional-looking prototypes quickly but consistently fall short when it comes to the engineering work required to turn those prototypes into production software. The author distinguishes between generating code that runs and building software that is maintainable, secure, and scalable — qualities that still require human judgment and expertise. The post draws on hands-on experience and positions itself against narratives suggesting AI can replace the full software development lifecycle.

stories.title: AI broke writing as proof-of-thought
stories.paragraph: A Substack essay argues that written work has traditionally served as evidence of cognitive effort — a way for readers to assess a writer's reasoning — and that AI-generated text dissolves this function by decoupling fluent prose from actual thought. The author frames this as a systemic epistemic problem, not merely a matter of academic dishonesty, because it affects how trust and credibility are established across professional and public communication. The piece does not propose a technical fix, instead focusing on the cultural consequences of losing writing as a reliable signal of human reasoning.

stories.title: Show HN: I worked on a new browser for 2 years, today it passed Acid 3
stories.paragraph: A developer shared CWBrowser, a new web browser they have been building independently for two years, which recently passed the Acid 3 web standards compliance test — a benchmark that measures how well a browser renders CSS, JavaScript, and other web technologies. Passing Acid 3 with a score of 100/100 is a meaningful milestone for a browser built outside of major corporate engineering teams. The project is hosted on Intellios AI's code platform and was submitted to Hacker News as a Show HN, inviting community feedback on the work.

stories.title: Thomson Reuters built its own AI model that now ranks among the best
stories.paragraph: Thomson Reuters has developed a proprietary large language model trained on its legal, tax, and regulatory data that it says now performs competitively against leading general-purpose models on domain-specific benchmarks. The move reflects a broader trend of large enterprises building in-house models rather than relying solely on third-party API access, citing data control and accuracy in specialized fields. Thomson Reuters is a major provider of legal research tools such as Westlaw, making domain accuracy a critical requirement for its AI deployments.

stories.title: smevals - a small eval suite for evaluating models, prompts, and harnesses
stories.paragraph: Simon Willison and Jesse Vincent's Prime Radiant applied AI research lab have released smevals, a lightweight evaluation framework designed to assess the capabilities of different language models, prompts, and harnesses. The tool allows users to run small, targeted eval suites and grade results, addressing a gap in accessible tooling for practitioners who need quick, reproducible comparisons without large-scale infrastructure. The project is openly available and documented on Willison's blog, with the aim of making model evaluation more approachable for individuals and small teams.

stories.title: Show HN: How to build and self-host a code review agent
stories.paragraph: Tilde, a side project developed over roughly one year, is an SDK platform that provides cloud API building blocks for constructing and self-hosting AI agents, with a code review agent offered as a concrete example use case. The project draws design ideas from existing harness frameworks such as OpenClaw and Hermes, attempting to decompose their best features into modular components. The self-hosting emphasis distinguishes Tilde from fully managed agent services, giving developers direct control over deployment and data handling.

stories.title: Show HN: Penca – branchable, versioned OLTP+OLAP on one open copy of your data
stories.paragraph: Penca is an early proof-of-concept database that combines transactional and analytical workloads on a single, open copy of data stored in object storage, while also supporting branching and versioning. The design is conceptually similar to Databricks' LTAP initiative, which aims to unify lake and transactional data access, but Penca is positioned as an open, self-hosted alternative. The project is at a pre-production stage, published on GitHub for community feedback and experimentation.

stories.title: Google withdraws new Earth AI tool after warnings over misinformation risks
stories.paragraph: Google has withdrawn a newly launched AI tool related to Google Earth following warnings from researchers and external parties about the risk of it generating or amplifying geographic misinformation. The withdrawal is notable because it represents a public rollback of a shipped product rather than a pre-launch cancellation, signaling that misinformation concerns can override deployment decisions even after release. The BBC report does not specify the exact mechanism by which the tool could produce misinformation, but the episode adds to ongoing scrutiny of AI products that interact with factual geographic and environmental data.

stories.title: EU tells firms to label AI-generated content from Sunday
stories.paragraph: The European Union has instructed companies operating in the bloc to label AI-generated content starting from Sunday, July 28, 2026, as part of the phased implementation of the EU AI Act. The requirement applies broadly to firms distributing AI-generated text, images, audio, and video to European users, and non-compliance could expose companies to regulatory penalties. The labeling mandate is one of the more visible consumer-facing obligations in the AI Act, which has been rolling out in stages since it came into force in 2024.

stories.title: Leopold Aschenbrenner built a $45B AI hedge fund lost most of it in days
stories.paragraph: Leopold Aschenbrenner, a former OpenAI researcher known for his "Situational Awareness" essay, launched an AI-focused hedge fund that reportedly reached approximately $45 billion in assets under management before suffering severe losses within a matter of days, according to CNBC. The fund is now reportedly in a fire-sale situation, with assets being liquidated. The episode highlights the financial risks of concentrated, thesis-driven investment strategies in the AI sector, where market conditions can shift rapidly.

stories.title: AI Is Getting Way Too Expensive
stories.paragraph: A piece in "Where's Your Ed At" argues that the cost of premium AI products has risen to a point that is becoming difficult to justify for many users and businesses, examining pricing trends across major AI subscriptions and API services. The author notes that several leading AI providers have introduced tiered pricing structures where the most capable models sit behind significantly higher price points than earlier offerings. The analysis raises questions about whether current pricing reflects actual cost structures or is driven by demand capture during a period of high user interest.

stories.title: Apple Will 'Watch Everything Burn' When AI Bubble Bursts
stories.paragraph: Analyst Horace Dediu, writing on Asymco, argues that Apple's measured approach to AI investment positions it to survive a potential correction in AI valuations that could damage more aggressively invested competitors. Dediu contends that Apple's characteristic strategy of entering markets late with tightly integrated products, rather than leading with speculative infrastructure spending, is a deliberate posture rather than a failure to keep up. The piece does not predict a specific timeline for a downturn but uses historical analogies from previous technology cycles to support its thesis.

stories.title: AI companies destroy rare and non recoverable physical books
stories.paragraph: An opinion piece in the Herald Scotland reports that AI companies engaged in large-scale data collection have been physically destroying rare and sometimes irreplaceable books in the process of digitizing them for training datasets. The author invokes the analogy of the burning of the Library of Alexandria to characterize the cultural stakes of losing physical artifacts that have no surviving digital or print copies. The piece does not name specific companies but describes a pattern of bulk acquisition and scanning operations where physical condition of materials is not preserved.

stories.title: Would you get tattooed just to interview at a 7-days-a-week AI startup?
stories.paragraph: An AI startup that reportedly required or encouraged job candidates to get a tattoo as part of its interview process has publicly admitted the stunt was reckless, following coverage by Ars Technica. The company, which operates on a seven-days-a-week work schedule, attracted attention for using the tattoo requirement as a signal of commitment and cultural fit. The incident has drawn criticism as an example of extreme workplace culture practices in the AI startup ecosystem.

stories.title: Hygon Reveals 512-Thread CPU and AI GPU to Rival Intel Xeon and Nvidia
stories.paragraph: Chinese chipmaker Hygon has announced a 512-thread CPU alongside an AI-focused GPU, positioning both products as alternatives to Intel's Xeon server processors and Nvidia's data center GPUs. Hygon, which traces its origins to a technology transfer agreement with AMD, has been developing its own chip portfolio partly in response to U.S. export restrictions that limit Chinese firms' access to leading-edge semiconductor products. The 512-thread specification places the CPU in the high-end server market, though independent performance benchmarks comparing it to current-generation Intel or AMD server chips have not yet been widely published.

stories.title: Google Earth's New AI Lets Anyone Fabricate Satellite Images
stories.paragraph: Google Earth has introduced an AI-powered feature that allows users to generate synthetic satellite imagery, raising concerns about the potential for fabricated geospatial content to be mistaken for real imagery. The capability is notable because satellite images have historically carried a strong presumption of documentary truth, often used as evidence in journalism, legal proceedings, and policy debates. The tool is accessible to general users without specialized knowledge, lowering the barrier to producing convincing false imagery of specific locations. This development adds to existing concerns about AI-generated media undermining trust in visual evidence.
